newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end mixed, curve flattens after ease.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end mixed, curve flattens after ease.

text.p: Canadian bonds were mixed at an early close on Friday, with longer term bonds more firmly bid after the Bank of Canada's 11th rate cut this year, analysts said.

"The long end had a really good bid all day," said one Toronto-based bond trader. "It tighened into the U.S., while a lot of the shorter stuff actually widened a bit. I think it's the only part that looks cheap now."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.15 to C$115.40 to yield 6.745 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark fell 10/32 to yield 6.51 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds was 24 basis points, unchanged from Thursday's close.

The Canadian yield curve flattened after the Bank of Canada cut its key bank rate by 25 basis points to 3.25 percent by intervening in the money market on Friday. The move effectively lowered the central bank's target range for the call loan or overnight lending rate to 2.75-3.25 from 3.0-3.5 percent.
Analysts said some dealers took advantage of the cut to sell shorter term bonds and buy higher yielding long-term issues.

"For the near term it seems like the Bank of Canada will be on hold. That means that a lot of people are moving out on the curve right now. Given how steep the Canadian curve is, the longer you go out, the better the value," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian analysts with New York-based financial analysis firm I.D.E.A.

The Toronto Bond Traders Association recommended an early 1500 EST (2000 GMT) closing today in light of Canada's Remembrance Day holiday on Monday. While bonds resume trading on Monday, many dealers will take the day off and volumes are expected to be light.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent of 2006 fell C$0.02 to C$106.35 to yield 6.143 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark fell 6/32 to yield 6.26 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds was 12 basis points, unchanged from Thursday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded at 2.88 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.17 percent.
